correctness.rationale: For p-values ∅ and W every term remains in the two-element constant subalgebra; for p=L leaf symmetry restricts outputs to ∅,L,W; for nonempty proper p=S⊂L the stabilizer has two leaf orbits, permitting only ∅,S,L\S,L,W. Thus at most 2·2·3·5=60. The co-implication C(A)=↑(W\A) detects whether an upset equals W, yielding four exclusive global case selectors. By gating suitable terms by these selectors every tuple of output choices is realized; cases disappear at m=0 and m=1, proving 4,12,60 exactly for every m. The checker independently implements worldwise quantified and bitset semantics over all upsets through m=5, constructs 60 normal forms, and generates the entire term algebra for m=0,1,2; it passed as packaged.

value.rationale: The exact smallest-variable term-function algebra is a natural benchmark for expressiveness over the concrete finite connected rooted stars already appearing in current bi-Esakia research. The sharp threshold between one and two leaves has a structural reason (a fourth mixed valuation type), a uniform formula normal form, and a complete equivalence decision method. The result is neither a generic count of all set maps nor a small case of a stated more general enumeration. It does not claim to settle unrestricted bi-intuitionistic free algebras.
